title: Maratha Empire
capsule: The Maratha Empire emerged from the guerrilla campaigns of Shivaji Bhonsle, who was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in June 1674 and wrested the Deccan from Mughal suzerainty; after Aurangzeb's death in 1707 the Marathas expanded rapidly across the subcontinent under Peshwa leadership. Baji Rao I (Peshwa 1720–1740) extended Maratha power north to Delhi and into Malwa and Gujarat; by 1760 the confederacy nominally controlled roughly 2.5 million km² from the Punjab to the Deccan. The Third Battle of Panipat (14 January 1761) against Ahmad Shah Durrani shattered Maratha military power in the north — among the dead were Vishwasrao, the Peshwa's son and heir, and the commander Sadashivrao Bhau — but the confederacy recovered. Three Anglo-Maratha Wars (1775–1782, 1803–1805, 1817–1818) progressively dismantled the empire; the final treaty following the Third War (1818) ended Peshwa rule and transferred most Maratha territories to the British East India Company.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Deccan heartland and major confederacy capitals are well-attested by Maratha administrative records (modin deshmukh documents), Persian chronicles, and British East India Company correspondence; the northern tributary reach in the Punjab and Rajputana fluctuated seasonally with campaign seasons and is imprecisely bounded in continental reconstructions.
